title: Beatrix and the Summer
premise: When pastry chef Lena Brightwater discovers her late grandmother co-signed the deed of Hollow Orchard vineyard with a woman she never mentioned—Beatrix Vane, who arrives demanding her half—the two estranged heirs are legally bound to run one harvest season together or lose everything to a predatory developer. As Lena fights to save her failing café and Beatrix wrestles with the family duty that once drove her away, their wary partnership deepens into something neither planned for. At the first harvest festival, they must choose between selling out separately and risking the whole heart together; they choose each other, merging café and orchard into one life rooted in found family.
about_author: Coral Eastwick is a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, orchards, and small towns where food is a language of its own. She lives near a cider orchard with her partner and an opinionated cat named Crumb.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A brutal morning at Brightwater Café: a final notice from the bank, a broken oven, and a loyal regulars' table that can't save her. She finds a lawyer's letter about an inheritance she never knew existed. Emotional beat: exhausted hope—a door opening in a wall she'd bricked up.

chapters.title: The Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the county records office she learns her grandmother co-owned Hollow Orchard with one Beatrix Vane—and that the property passes to both names jointly. The developer Marlowe Group is circling. Beat: unease; the safe life was built on an omission.

chapters.title: A Woman in the Driveway
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix arrives at the orchard after twelve years away, armed with a deed and old resentments toward the grandmother who cut her out. She meets Lena, who mistakes her for a trespasser. Beat: friction and instant, unwelcome recognition.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The lawyer explains the clause: joint owners must operate the orchard through one full season or the estate defaults to sale—to the Marlowe Group, naturally. They agree to a truce of ninety days. Beat: reluctant alliance, sparks under sarcasm.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Walking the overgrown rows, Beatrix confronts memories of the grandfather who taught her grafting and the fight that made her leave. Lena shows up with pastries instead of an apology. Beat: grief softening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Flour and Frost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A late frost threatens the blossom; the women work all night lighting smudge pots side by side. Lena learns Beatrix abandoned a corporate career, not just a family. Beat: first real tenderness, disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Regulars' Table
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena's café family—waitress Dot, baker Sam, retired teacher Mr. Okafor—show up uninvited to help prune, adopting Beatrix without permission. Beat: found family forming around them both; Beatrix unnerved by belonging.

chapters.title: Marlowe Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A slick Marlowe rep offers each woman a separate buyout—enough to erase Lena's debt outright. Beatrix hides the size of her own offer. Beat: temptation and the first secret between them.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the farmhouse attic they find years of letters between their grandmothers—former lovers whose falling-out split the families. The parallel lands hard. Beat: revelation reframing everything; fear of repeating history.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A summer storm flattines the trellises; insurance won't cover it. Working shoulder to shoulder in the mud, Beatrix catches Lena when she falls. Beat: adrenaline-bonded intimacy, almost-kiss interrupted by Sam.

chapters.title: The Café Closes Its Doors
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The bank calls the loan; Lena signs over the lease, hollowed out. Beatrix finds her packing and stays the night—not romantically, just present. Beat: rock bottom met with unexpected gentleness.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Owes
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Flashback chapter: the duty-bound engagement Beatrix fled, the father who called the orchard a graveyard, why she never came back even for the funeral. Beat: self-forgiveness beginning; understanding what running cost her.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The grapes begin to ripen; so does everything unsaid. A harvest-planning evening turns into dancing in the barn, then the first kiss. Beat: surrender—but morning brings Beatrix's retreat.

chapters.title: The Second Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Marlowe returns with a deadline and a threat: contest the deed's validity using Beatrix's long absence as abandonment. Terrified of losing by law what she might win by love, Beatrix considers taking the money and going. Beat: fear masquerading as self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: Pieces Lent, Pieces Kept
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confronts Beatrix: 'You lend pieces so you never owe the whole.' Beatrix admits the Marlowe threat and her plan to sell. Devastated, Lena tells her to go. Beat: the wound of loving someone mid-flight.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix signs nothing but drives to her father's house to end the old bargain face-to-face—choosing herself, not the escape route. She returns to find the whole found family holding the orchard together in her absence. Beat: courage; homecoming.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marlowe contests the deed before the county board. Grandmother's letters, neighbors' testimony, and the season's labor argue the orchard is lived-in, loved, and jointly worked. Beat: public stakes, private declarations made in testimony.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They win—but barely, and broke. The community turns out for the first harvest: picking, pressing, Lena's pop-up pastry stand under the trees. Beat: joy earned; the two women choosing each other openly among everyone.

chapters.title: Cider and Confession
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Night after the festival, Beatrix gives Lena the letter she wrote and never sent three years ago, and asks—not for forgiveness—for the chance to stay. Beat: vulnerability answered with the whole heart.

chapters.title: Brightwater & Vane
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Winter planning: a combined café-cidery on the orchard grounds, Dot managing front of house, Sam on bread, Mr. Okafor keeping books. The grandmothers' letters framed above the counter. Beat: building a future from mended things.

chapters.title: What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Spring pruning, one year on. Beatrix grafts new stock onto the grandmother's oldest rootstock—old wood, new growth. Lena realizes she stopped counting safe steps somewhere along the way. Beat: quiet, rooted happiness.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Summer
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The second harvest opens with the renamed business thriving and the Marlowe Group long gone. On the farmhouse porch, Beatrix proposes with a ring hidden in a flour tin. Beat: full-circle resolution—love chosen against every easier exit, and kept.
